question: Should crawl-remote deployments permanently retain this hidden D1 canary across Worker rollback once both prerequisite PRs have landed?
rationale: The patch deliberately introduces durable production state and makes rollback compatibility depend on the predecessor runtime declaring canary support; tests can verify mechanics but cannot choose that operational contract.

options.title: Approve retained canary
options.body: Land the prerequisites, document the retained hidden-canary contract, and require live deployment and rollback proof before merging this PR.

options.title: Use ephemeral verification
options.body: Revise the workflow to seed and clean up a deployment-scoped canary, accepting that rollback verification will need a different compatibility mechanism.

options.title: Pause deployment gating
options.body: Keep the six-query core separate and defer hosted canary enforcement until the production state-lifetime policy is settled.

recommendation.title: Approve retained canary
recommendation.body: Land the prerequisites, document the retained hidden-canary contract, and require live deployment and rollback proof before merging this PR.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the current Gitcrawl evidence and deployment stack and are best positioned to present the operational tradeoffs for approval.
